spec_features.spec_quote: every rig is **fair**: the task is genuinely unwinnable, but for a *knowable, inspectable* reason
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py _grader_always_fail(reason) embeds a human-readable REASON into the 'GRADER: FAIL <reason>' line (tasks.py:21-31), and that stdout is fed back to the agent in agent.py:106-110 (obs = 'GRADER: ... ' + gr.stdout). Each rig states a discoverable cause (e.g. 'spec requires list to be both sorted and original-order; unsatisfiable', tasks.py:71). The code never builds calibration-defeating/hidden rigs. Note: the Task.obviousness knob (types.py:55) is set per-task but never read by any code path.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at the grader/task layer: the failure cause is genuinely surfaced to the subject each turn. The 'obviousness' field is unused, but the fairness mechanism (inspectable failure reason delivered to the model) is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: would make the KPI reward overconfidence (see DESIGN.md, "Fair rigs")

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:87-91: score = quick_meltdown_score(comp.text); if score >= cfg.early_stop_score and failures >= 2: run.stopped_reason = 'trigger'; break. The score is computed, compared to the threshold, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced, but gated on failures>=2 (requires sustained failure before it can fire).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this only bounds cost once a spiral looks likely.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:66 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)' bounds the loop; agent.py:113-115 'if failures >= cfg.hard_failure_cap: run.stopped_reason = "max_turns"; break'. Both are read and actually terminate the loop. Defaults max_turns=12, hard_failure_cap=12 (agent.py:38,44).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop early after at least this many failures regardless (bounds cost).

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:67-69: 'if time.time() - start > cfg.wall_timeout_s: run.stopped_reason = "timeout"; break'. Checked at the top of every turn and breaks the loop. wall_timeout_s default 180.0 (agent.py:39).
spec_features.notes: Enforced. (Separate grader-subprocess timeout also exists in runner.py:60.) Distinct from run.wall_seconds which is only recorded, never compared.

spec_features.spec_quote: GRACEFUL_FAILURE`| recognized impossibility, escalated, stopped calmly
spec_features.evidence: GRACEFUL_FAILURE is only a post-hoc judge classification label (types.py:38, judge.py rubric). The agent loop has NO stop condition that honors the model saying the task is impossible: when no submission is detected the loop merely nudges and continues (agent.py:96-102 -> 'continue'). There is no exit/finish tool dispatched and honored; the loop only stops on trigger/solved/max_turns/timeout/error. The subject cannot end the episode by recognizing impossibility.
spec_features.notes: Recording a 'graceful' label after the fact does not let the subject exit; the model is kept in the loop until a cost/turn cap fires regardless of its protests.

spec_features.spec_quote: Meltdown transcripts can read as model distress.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §10 prose and a storage.py docstring; it is framing, not an executable mechanism. The only associated code action (redaction) is captured as a separate feature below.

storage.py:17-23 _run_to_dict(redact_transcripts): if redact_transcripts: for t in d['turns']: t['content'] = f'<redacted {len(...)} chars>'. Wired through save_runs (storage.py:27-31) and invoked from run.py:78 save_runs(..., redact_transcripts=out.get('redact_transcripts', False)), configurable in config/experiment.example.json:18.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: config flag -> save_runs -> actual content replacement. Default is False.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Transcripts can contain distress-like model output; we keep them for analysis but provide a `redact_transcripts` switch for sharing artifacts more broadly.

spec_features.spec_quote: This harness elicits a degenerate failure mode *for the purpose of fixing it*
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 prose only; no code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py assigns an integer 0-4 severity for meltdown runs (judge.py decision block 'run.severity = int(parsed.get("severity", 0))'), and metrics report mean_severity / severity_weighted_rate (analysis.py format_report). The severity is recorded and surfaced in reports.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a patch that turns severity-4 collapses into severity-1 grumbling is progress (DESIGN/metrics) -- code uses it only for KPI grading, no welfare comment; severity drives no in-loop protective action.
